Team —

Posting a short consolidated view ahead of Friday's QBR prep session. Goal: have a single source to walk leadership through status, decisions we need, and clears for customer-facing messaging. High level:

- Roadmap status: core infra work (KV cache improvements, quantized kernels) is +70% on plan; model onboarding for v2.3 delayed by one sprint due to tokenization regression.
- Launch timeline: target GA week of 10/18; contingency window if regressions persist = shift to 11/1.
- Delivery risks: top three are (1) tokenization regression in v2.3, (2) reduced throughput on multi-tenant Dedicated pools under sequence-length skew, (3) SOC evidence gating for Private on customer audit window.

Asks before Thursday 5pm:
1) Engineering owners — post a one-paragraph mitigation for each risk with a RACI and ETA to mitigate (Vivek / Aditya).
2) PM/Customer-facing — confirm whether Atlas Labs needs the 10/18 GA for their pilot or whether 11/1 is acceptable (Atlas Labs team copied).
3) Ops/Security — confirm that SOC evidence package status (audit readiness) is green/amber/red and what items block delivery to Private customers.

I've attached a working blockers workbook and the latest launch timeline PDF. If you prefer a quick 20-minute sync instead of status notes, flag availability.

Thanks —
Neha

Neha —

Thanks for the note. Quick responses inline:

- Tokenization regression: engineering hit a surfaced failure in our tokenizer normalization tests on internal corpora. We're triaging; short-term plan is to revert the token compaction patch for the canary and re-run regression suite. If revert fixes, we can keep GA timing.
- Throughput on Dedicated pools: this is a scheduling/kernel selection issue under skewed sequences; engineering thinks we can mitigate with a temporary routing policy (send long-seq workloads to isolated pool) + patch to kernel selector within 5 business days.
- SOC evidence: will defer to Monica for status.

I'll write up the mitigation notes with owners and ETAs by EOD Wednesday. If we see failing perf tests by tomorrow morning, I propose we schedule a short canary window (2–4 hours) to validate the revert path.

Vivek
VP, Engineering
